Degrees of Uncertainty when Talking About the Past
All modal perfect verbs refer to the past. You can use them to express different degrees of uncertainty.

When you want to talk about cause and effect, there are different ways to go about it. You can use a conjunction like because to express the reason or cause of the effect (result).

You can place the cause-clause (because + clause) before or after the effect-clause.

For example:
The children were happy because they received presents.
Because they received presents, the children were happy.

Notice that you use a comma when the cause-clause comes before the effect-clause.
I hope everyone stays home because the snow doesn't look like it's letting up.
Maybe he decided to stay at home because the weather is dreadful.
Sally had a birthday party planned at a restaurant on a Saturday because she thought people wouldn't come to a party on that Sunday.
Because it was raining, they decided to stay home.
But nobody came Saturday because she had mixed up the dates on the invitations.

images.text:
Peter: How much should we play for?
Vanessa: How about for the money you already owe me?
Peter: Heh heh. Amy I forgot to ask, you invited a few of your friends to come out tonight, right?
Amy: Yeah, Jane, who works in my office, wasn't feeling well yesterday. She must have caught a cold, so she didn't want to come out and my other friend Terri didn't answer the phone when I called her. She must have fallen asleep.

Vanessa: I talked to Jose about coming out, but he might have forgotten.
Peter: He can't have forgotten. I sent him a text earlier tonight and he said he would make an appearance.
Vanessa: Maybe he decided to stay at home because the weather is dreadful.

Peter: Good. I hope everyone stays home because the snow doesn't look like it's letting up.
Vanessa: Peter, do you remember Sally's birthday party when no one showed up?
Peter: Sadly.
Amy: Oh no! What happened?
Vanessa: Sally had a birthday party planned at a restaurant on Saturday because she thought people wouldn't come to a party on that Sunday which was her actual birthday.

Peter: She made up a big list of people, sent out invitations to everyone and booked a restaurant. It was going to be a gala evening.
Vanessa: Ohhh! But nobody came Saturday because she had mixed up the dates on the invitations.
Amy: Ohhh! Poor girl! As she was sitting there, wondering where her friends were, she must have felt pretty dejected.
Peter: She said initially, she was feeling pretty irate since no one had come to her party that she worked so hard on to plan.
Amy: What did she do?
Vanessa: She started phoning people and she quickly figured out the mistake. We were able to rebook the next day at nearly the same time, so it all worked out.
Amy: Alright I'm ready. Let's play some … oh no!
Vanessa: The power is out!
Peter: Yep, it's a blackout!
